latest.title: Staffing, in hours and days you can act on
latest.summary: The staffing plan now builds a week one person can really work. Nobody is spread across two businesses, hours stay inside the full-time band the game pays for, and somebody who asked for four days a week gets four, not five. A shop the board cannot read yet says so and covers its cleaning and security in the meantime, instead of offering to clear a schedule that nothing here could put back. The block is now called Staffing and speaks the game's own language: hours and days rather than shifts, entries you copy into BizMan one day at a time, stations by name with the short codes on hover, and people to hire rather than posts, each sized at the 30 hours a week a full-time employee is owed. It also says what makes its numbers worth reading, which is two weeks with every station staffed. Building capacity replaces "door cap" on the board and in the location finder.
